subject: Accelerant (NebulaOps) — late-stage capacity precheck & soft hold request
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Accelerant (NebulaOps) — late-stage capacity precheck & soft hold request

Team —

NebulaOps is at contract signature (we expect counters by EOW) and asked if we can provisionally reserve capacity while legal/PO complete. Summary: 
- Account: NebulaOps (Accelerant POC -> GA)
- Ask: Soft hold for 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (or 12 H100 equiv) for Aug 1 — Sep 30 (initial two-month runway)
- Workload: mix of high-QPS inference (batch size 1–4) and occasional model warm-up training runs; expected sustained 1.2k infer/sec across cluster, p95 latency target <120ms.

Can you do a quick inventory/availability check in the US west pools and confirm: 1) whether we can put a soft hold (no billing) until 2025-07-02, 2) what node/pool names match the ask, and 3) any recommended alternative sizing (e.g., H100 vs A100 split) if capacity is tight?

Attached: accelerant-mop-v2.xlsx (from SE: target qps & traffic windows). Need an ops-facing answer for Nebula by EOD tomorrow so sales can advise procurement.

Short answers welcome — I can triage followups.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Deals | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Accelerant (NebulaOps) — late-stage capacity precheck & soft hold request

Hey Steph —

Quick read: we have some flex in US-west pools but need a few clarifications before committing even a soft hold. Questions:
1) Is the 1.2k infer/sec steady across 24h or spiky (daily peak windows)?
2) Do they require data isolation (dedicated pool) vs shared-dedicated slice? Procurement usually asks for dedicated capacity on enterprise deals.
3) Any firm preference for GPU family (A100 vs H100)? H100s are scarcer in some zones.

Initial signal: I can cover a soft hold of 12 A100-equivalent units across zone-w1 and zone-w2 assuming no more than 6 units reserved per zone. If they need 16 contiguous in the same zone, we may need a fallback plan (hybrid A100/H100 or split across zones).

I'll pull fleet inventory and send a snapshot (fleet-inventory-20250618.csv) and list candidate pools.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 12:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerant (NebulaOps) — late-stage capacity precheck & soft hold request

Attaching the inventory snapshot I just exported (fleet-inventory-20250618.csv). Quick read and my recommendations below.

On Tue, Jun 19, 2025 at 10:03 AM Ben Carter wrote:
> Hey Steph —
> 
> Quick read: we have some flex in US-west pools but need a few clarifications before committing even a soft hold. Questions:
> 1) Is the 1.2k infer/sec steady across 24h or spiky (daily peak windows)?
> 2) Do they require data isolation (dedicated pool) vs shared-dedicated slice? Procurement usually asks for dedicated capacity on enterprise deals.
> 3) Any firm preference for GPU family (A100 vs H100)? H100s are scarcer in some zones.

Answers we already got from SE/AE (from the attached MOP):
- Traffic shape: predictable daily peaks (09:00–11:00 and 18:00–20:00 PT) — steady baseline ~650 infer/sec with peaks to ~1.8k for ~45–90 minutes.
- Isolation: They requested a dedicated pool for compliance reasons (audit logs + KMS integration).
- GPU family: Prefers H100 if available; acceptable on A100-equivalent with a small performance delta.

Sizing rationale: to meet p95 <120ms in a dedicated pool with the given peaks and latency SLO, we should plan for 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (or 12 H100 equiv) to cover warm-up and headroom. However, because they want dedicated isolation, contiguous single-zone allocation is preferred for network/disk locality.

Availability summary (US-west):
- pool-west-1-dedicated (H100): 8 free units
- pool-west-1-dedicated (A100): 6 free units
- pool-west-2-dedicated (A100): 10 free units

Recommendation:
1) Create a soft-hold ticket scoped to ACCEL-2025-0921 to reserve 8 H100 + 8 A100-equivalent across pool-west-1 / pool-west-2 with preference for pool-west-1 contiguous allocation. This gives us immediate headroom of 16 A100-eq.
2) If Nebula insists on same-zone contiguous 16 H100s, we need to propose hybrid plan with auto-fallback to pool-west-2 A100s and an SLA note about performance variance.
3) Put a 14-day soft hold expiry (no billing) to align with procurement cadence and revisit on 2025-07-03.

I'm copying Marissa for rollout coordination and to flag any capacity commitments that might conflict with upcoming Q3 reserved capacity sales.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Kim <laura.kim@nebulaops.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nebulaops.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Accelerant (NebulaOps) — late-stage capacity precheck & soft hold request

Thanks, Stephanie / team — this is helpful. A couple quick replies: 
1) Dedicated pool is required (compliance + KMS).
2) We prefer H100 for expected model versions, but will accept mixed family if you document the fallback performance delta.
3) 14-day soft hold is fine — please include a note in the HubSpot deal that the hold expires 2025-07-03 unless a PO/contract signature is received.

Procurement: attaching our standard PO window; can you send a DocuSign for a provisional capacity acknowledgement that doesnt bill until hold activation?

Laura Kim
Head of Platform Engineering | NebulaOps
